x-m-e2-01.title: Find Suji secret number

x-m-e2-01.material:

x-m-e2-01.thinking.2: Compare clues to choose di one wey narrow answer down to one

x-m-e2-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose all numbers out of four wey fit be Suji number. (E must meet all three clues.)

x-m-e2-01.s.s1.r.b: If you choose 642: you check di three clues place by place. If you miss am, check each clue again with place names.
x-m-e2-01.s.s1.r.c: If you choose 353: you see relationship between tens and ones correct, but maybe no check clue comparing hundreds and tens.
x-m-e2-01.s.s1.r.d: If you choose 975: you check clues place by place. If you miss am, test all three clues on this number one by one.
x-m-e2-01.s.s1.explain: 420 get 0 for ones place, so e break clue 2; 353 get 3 for hundreds, less than 5 for tens, so e break clue 3. 642 and 975 meet all three clues.

x-m-e2-01.s.s2.hint.0: If you choose ones digit first, tens digit go decide. Then think about hundreds place.
x-m-e2-01.s.s2.hint.1: Test numbers you make against clues 1, 2, and 3 one by one.
x-m-e2-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Hundreds digit must be one-digit number from 1 to 9.
x-m-e2-01.s.s2.ok.c2: Tens and ones places na one-digit numbers.
x-m-e2-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Tens and ones digits must be one-digit numbers from 0 to 9.
x-m-e2-01.s.s2.ok.c3: Tens digit pass ones digit by 2.
x-m-e2-01.s.s2.fail.c3: Check again whether tens digit pass ones digit by 2.
x-m-e2-01.s.s2.fail.c5: Check whether hundreds digit pass tens digit.
x-m-e2-01.s.s2.explain: For example, 431, 642, and 975. If you choose ones digit from 1 to 7, tens digit go decide; for hundreds place you fit choose any digit wey pass am. Plenty numbers dey possible, so you need more clues.
x-m-e2-01.s.s3.prompt: Suji give one more clue. Which clue, once you hear am, go narrow secret number down to exactly one?

x-m-e2-01.s.s3.hint.1: Compare how many numbers remain for each clue.
x-m-e2-01.s.s3.r.a: Dis clue alone leave plenty choices for tens digit, from 3 to 8. You need count by yourself how many numbers clue narrow am down to.
x-m-e2-01.s.s3.o.b: Di three digits add up to 12
x-m-e2-01.s.s3.r.b: Good if you find every case wey sum na 12, but if you only find one and stop, check more to see whether other cases remain.
x-m-e2-01.s.s3.r.c: You think say once ones place decide, other clues go give tens and hundreds places.

x-m-e2-02.title: Which one of two three-digit numbers bigger?
x-m-e2-02.goal: Use counterexample to show claim no always correct, and explain say number size depend on comparing from highest place, no be digit sum.
x-m-e2-02.material: Hayun wan find which of two three-digit numbers bigger, and write solution her own way.
x-m-e2-02.prereq.0: Experience comparing three-digit numbers and place value (hundreds, tens, ones)
x-m-e2-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose line for Hayun solution where wrong thinking first show. (Count from line 1.)
x-m-e2-02.s.s1.hint.0: Sort each line as "calculation" or "conclusion from calculation."
x-m-e2-02.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether calculation result for line above correct, and whether you fit decide which bigger from that result.
x-m-e2-02.s.s1.line.0: Make we check which bigger: 399 or 401.
x-m-e2-02.s.s1.line.3: So for two three-digit numbers, di one wey digit sum bigger na di bigger number.
x-m-e2-02.s.s1.explain: First mistake dey line 3. Addition for line 2 correct, but you no suppose decide size from digit sum. 399 get 3 hundreds and 401 get 4 hundreds, so 401 bigger. Line 4 expand idea from line 3 to "always", so e follow di mistake.
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.prompt: Make examples wey Hayun method wrong. Find number x wey digit sum bigger but number actually smaller, and number y wey digit sum smaller but number bigger. Make two pairs.
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.hint.0: Think of numbers wey hundreds digit small but tens and ones digits big.
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.hint.1: Check both say digit sum of x bigger than y and x smaller than y.
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.var.x: Number x, whose digit sum bigger but e smaller
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.var.y: Number y, whose digit sum smaller but e bigger
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.fail.c1: x must be three-digit number (100 to 999).
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.fail.c2: y must be three-digit number (100 to 999).
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.fail.c3: Check whether x smaller than y. Compare starting from hundreds place.
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.ok.c4: Digit sum of x bigger than digit sum of y.
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.fail.c4: Recalculate whether sum of all digits in x pass sum of all digits in y.
x-m-e2-02.s.s2.explain: For 399 and 401, digit sums na 21 and 5, but 399 smaller. For 199 and 310, sums na 19 and 4, but 199 smaller. Even one example wey method wrong show say "always" no hold.
x-m-e2-02.s.s3.prompt: So when comparing size of two three-digit numbers, which place you suppose look first? Write reason too.
x-m-e2-02.s.s3.hint.0: Think about value each digit stand for (hundreds, tens, ones).
x-m-e2-02.s.s3.hint.1: For 399 and 401, look from highest place to find which place different.
x-m-e2-02.s.s3.placeholder: For example: You must compare from ... because ...
x-m-e2-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You connect reason for starting at hundreds place with "how many hundreds dey"?
x-m-e2-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write wetin to do if hundreds places equal?
x-m-e2-02.s.s3.model.0: Compare from hundreds digit. If hundreds digits differ, bigger digit mean bigger number; if dem same, compare tens digits.
x-m-e2-02.s.s3.model.1: You must first look at hundreds place, di leftmost digit. 399 get 3 hundreds and 401 get 4, so 401 bigger. Only if hundreds places same you check tens place.
x-m-e2-02.s.s3.model.2: 399 and 401 differ for hundreds place, 3 and 4, so answer decide there. Digit for higher place mean bigger value.

x-m-e2-03.title: Where borrowed 10 go?
x-m-e2-03.topic: Why addition and subtraction calculations dey work
x-m-e2-03.goal: Find mistake for solution wey forget say digit change for place we borrow from, explain why we check with addition and give correct solution.
x-m-e2-03.material: Na Seojin vertical calculation of 342−158. Read solution and find wetin strange.
x-m-e2-03.thinking.1: Evaluating way to check calculation result
x-m-e2-03.thinking.2: Explain cause of error with your own words
x-m-e2-03.prereq.0: Practice vertical calculation of three-digit numbers (line up places)
x-m-e2-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose line where Seojin solution first go wrong. (Count from line 1.)
x-m-e2-03.s.s1.hint.0: For each place, check in order whether digit written match calculation for line before.
x-m-e2-03.s.s1.hint.1: For every line, use table to write which number dem subtract from, how much dem subtract, and how much dem borrow.
x-m-e2-03.s.s1.line.1: Ones place: You no fit remove 8 from 2, so borrow 10 from tens place and write 12−8=4.
x-m-e2-03.s.s1.line.2: Tens place: You no fit remove 5 from 4, so borrow 10 from hundreds place and write 14−5=9.
x-m-e2-03.s.s1.line.3: Hundreds place: Remove 1 wey 3 lend to get 2, then subtract 1 from 2 and write 1.
x-m-e2-03.s.s1.explain: Line 3 na first mistake. For line 2, 4 for tens place lend 10 to ones place, so tens place become 3. For line 3, you no fit remove 5 from 3, so borrow from hundreds and write 13−5=8.
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.prompt: Seojin wan check whether answer 194 correct. Which method show in convincing way say e wrong?
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.hint.0: Think about calculation paired with subtraction wey undo am.
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.hint.1: Think one by one whether each method check with different route from first solution.
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.o.a: Calculate again the same way and see if same value come out
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.r.a: If you calculate again with same idea, you fit repeat same mistake. Check with another method.
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.o.b: Add 158 to answer 194 and see if e be 342
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.r.b: Dis check use relationship say subtraction answer plus number removed give starting number. Think too why relationship hold.
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.r.c: Subtracting 158 from answer make new subtraction, so hard to compare direct with original expression. Think if e connect to expression you wan check.
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.o.d: Check only whether ones digit 4 correct
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.r.d: Even if the ones place correct, other places fit wrong. Checking one place no check everything.
x-m-e2-03.s.s2.explain: 194+158=352, no be 342. Answer to subtraction plus the number wey you subtract suppose equal the starting number, so if you get 352, 194 wrong.
x-m-e2-03.s.s3.prompt: Wetin be the correct answer? Write where and why Seojin make mistake too.
x-m-e2-03.s.s3.hint.0: Write how the tens digit change after e lend 10 to the ones place.
x-m-e2-03.s.s3.hint.1: After you write your answer, calculate directly with the checking method you choose before to see whether e correct.
x-m-e2-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You explain why the tens digit become 3 and no be 4?
x-m-e2-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You use addition check the correct answer wey you write?
x-m-e2-03.s.s3.model.0: Na 184. The tens place lend 10 to the ones place, so e become 3, no be 4. You no fit take 5 from 3, so you must borrow again from the hundreds place.
x-m-e2-03.s.s3.model.1: 184 correct. The 4 lend 1, so e become 3. You no fit take 5 from 3, so you need bring 10 from the hundreds place, but Seojin just subtract from 4.

x-m-e2-04.title: Wetin information we really need?

x-m-e2-05.title: When you never memorize 7×6
x-m-e2-05.topic: Multiplication facts and counting in groups
x-m-e2-05.goal: Judge whether methods for finding multiplication answer wey you no know from one wey you know correct, by thinking wetin "this many groups of this many" mean.
x-m-e2-05.material: The friends for one group no remember the answer to 7×6. Dem imagine 6 bags with 7 candies each and suggest five methods. Dem talk say dem already know 7×5=35, 6×6=36, 7×3=21, and 7×7=49.
x-m-e2-05.thinking.0: Judging whether different methods correct and giving reasons
x-m-e2-05.thinking.1: Explaining why a wrong method wrong by using the meaning of groups
x-m-e2-05.prereq.0: Meaning of multiplication (this many groups of this many) and some experience memorizing multiplication facts
x-m-e2-05.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the methods wey give the correct answer.
x-m-e2-05.s.s1.hint.0: Picture how many bags of 7 candies dey, as if you dey draw am.
x-m-e2-05.s.s1.hint.1: For each method, check whether the number dem add or subtract na the "number of bags" or the "number of candies inside one bag."
x-m-e2-05.s.s1.r.a: If you choose this method: you think say one extra bag add 7. If you miss am, think wetin increase when one more bag dey.
x-m-e2-05.s.s1.r.b: If you choose this method: maybe you think to add the 6 from "6 bags." Wetin increase, number of bags or number of candies?
x-m-e2-05.s.s1.r.c: If you choose this method: you think say joining candies from 3 bags two times make 6 bags. If you miss am, count how many bags 3 bags two times make.
x-m-e2-05.s.s1.r.d: If you choose this method: the idea to remove one bag from 7 bags correct, but you no check wetin dem remove.
x-m-e2-05.s.s1.r.e: If you choose this method: you use the fact say 7×6 and 6×7 na the same. If you miss am, think of am as 7 bags with 6 inside each.
x-m-e2-05.s.s1.explain: Adding one bag (7) to 7×5=35 give 42; doubling 7×3=21 give 42; adding 6 to 6×6=36 give 42, so all of dem correct. Adding 6 to 7×5 give 41, and subtracting 6 from 7×7=49 give 43, so dem wrong. When number of bags increase or reduce by one, the total increase or reduce by the number of candies inside one bag (7).
x-m-e2-05.s.s2.prompt: Why the method "add 6 to the answer for 7×5" wrong? Explain with candies and bags.

x-m-e2-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You talk how many candies get added when one more bag dey?
x-m-e2-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You compare how many bags 7×5 get and how many bags 7×6 get?
x-m-e2-05.s.s2.model.0: Na 6 groups of 7, but 7×5 na 5 groups. If one more group dey, you must add 7 more, so add 7, no be 6.
x-m-e2-05.s.s2.model.1: 7×5 na 7 wey you add 5 times. To make am 6 times, add 7 one more time. But if you add 6, e increase by only 6, no be 7, so e wrong.
x-m-e2-05.s.s2.model.2: Each bag get 7, so you suppose add 7, but dem add only 6, so e wrong.

x-m-e2-06.thinking.0: Using skip-counting to judge whether sharing equally go work
x-m-e2-06.thinking.1: Making several ways wey meet the conditions
x-m-e2-06.thinking.2: Explaining why the cases wey no meet the conditions no work
x-m-e2-06.prereq.0: Multiplication facts (2 times table to 9 times table), and experience skip-counting by different numbers
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.prompt: If you put 5 marbles inside each bag, you fit share all 24 marbles equally with nothing left?
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.hint.0: Count by 5 and check whether you reach 24.
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.hint.1: "Share equally" mean every bag get the same number.
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.o.a: Yes. Put the 4 wey remain inside one more bag
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.r.a: If you choose this: you think say "put everything inside" and "share equally" na the same. Check whether the last bag get 5 too.
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.o.b: No. If you count by 5, 25 come after 20, so you jump over 24
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.r.b: If you choose this: you use skip-counting check whether you reach 24. Think whether you fit check other numbers this way too.
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.o.c: Yes. Remove only 1 from 5 bags of 5 and dem go become equal
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.r.c: If you choose this: you see say 25 and 24 close, so small change go do. Check whether removing 1 make only one bag get 4.
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.o.d: No. 5 na odd number, so you no fit share 24 equally
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.r.d: If you choose this: you think say odd numbers no work. Count the case wey you put 3 in each bag to check.
x-m-e2-06.s.s1.explain: When you count by 5, you get 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, so you pass 24; you no fit share equally with 5 inside each bag. But odd number 3 work too, because 3×8=24, so being odd no mean say e no go work.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.prompt: Choose number of marbles inside each bag, a, and number of bags, b, then find all ways to share 24 equally. Conditions: a and b na numbers from the multiplication table (from 2 to 9), and number of marbles in one bag, a, must bigger than number of bags, b.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.hint.0: Find two numbers from multiplication table wey their product na 24.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.hint.1: From the two numbers you find, use the condition to decide which one na number inside each bag and which one na number of bags.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.var.a: Number of marbles inside one bag
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.ok.c1: Both numbers na whole numbers from 2 to 9.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.fail.c1: a and b must be whole numbers from 2 to 9.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.fail.c2: Check whether a multiplied by b make 24.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.ok.c3: Number of marbles inside one bag bigger than number of bags.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.fail.c3: Check whether number of marbles in one bag, a, bigger than number of bags, b.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.explain: The multiplication facts wey give product 24 na 3×8, 4×6, 6×4, and 8×3. Of these, the cases wey number of marbles in one bag bigger than number of bags na 4 bags with 6 each, and 3 bags with 8 each. So two ways dey.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.because.prompt: Why you no fit use the way to share dem into 12 bags of 2 under these conditions?
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.because.hint.1: Read again the two conditions wey the question give for a and b.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You talk which of the two conditions (numbers from 2 to 9, more marbles than bags) e no follow?
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You also know say 2×12=24, so dem share the marbles correctly?
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.because.model.0: If you put 2 inside each bag, you need 12 bags, so number of bags become more than number of marbles per bag. And 12 no dey inside the multiplication table either.
x-m-e2-06.s.s2.because.model.1: 2×12=24, so na 12 bags, but 12 no dey inside multiplication table up to 9 times table, so e no work.

x-m-e2-07.title: Seoa measure the length correctly?
x-m-e2-07.goal: Learn say when you measure length with ruler, the mark at one end no enough to know the length, then make method and example to find length when the starting mark no be 0.
x-m-e2-07.material: Seoa and Doyun dey measure pencil length with 15cm ruler. The ruler get marks from 0 to 15, and the space between neighboring marks na 1cm.
x-m-e2-07.thinking.0: Holding off judgment when information no enough
x-m-e2-07.thinking.1: Changing your judgment when new information come
x-m-e2-07.thinking.2: Making mark positions wey match the conditions
x-m-e2-07.prereq.0: Experience reading centimeters (cm) and marks on ruler
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.prompt: Arrange your thinking each time new information come.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.hint.0: First think whether you fit decide the length with only the information wey you know now.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.hint.1: Look which end position the new information tell you about.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.0.info: After measuring pencil length with ruler, Seoa talk, "The pencil long reach 11cm." The marks for this ruler start from 0, and the right end of pencil touch mark 11. She never talk where the left end of pencil dey yet.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.0.ask: Wetin you think about wetin Seoa talk now?
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.0.after: The length no depend only on the mark at one end. You need know which mark both ends dey on.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Correct. The end touch mark 11, so e long reach 11cm
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You only look at the mark wey the end touch. Think whether you need know the other end too to find the length.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.0.o.b: I no know. I need see where the other end dey
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You think say length mean measuring the space between the two ends.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Wrong. Na pencil, so e probably shorter than 11cm
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You decide based on the usual size of pencil. Think whether you fit decide without information.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.1.info: Doyun look carefully and talk, "The left end of the pencil no dey mark 0; e dey mark 2."
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.1.ask: So how long the pencil be?
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.1.after: From mark 2 to 11 na 9 spaces of 1cm, so e long reach 9cm. Seoa wrong because she no check whether the left end dey 0.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You add 2 and 11. Think how to find di distance between both ends.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You read only di right end, like say you measure from mark 0. Remember say di left end no dey at 0.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You count how many 1cm spaces dey from mark 2 to mark 11.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.info: Seoa tell you how another pencil measure. Di pencil left end dey at mark 3 and di right end dey at mark 8.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.ask: Choose all correct ways to find di length of dis pencil.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.after: From mark 3 to 8 get 5 spaces, so e na 5cm. Whether you count di spaces or subtract small mark from big mark, you get di same answer.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Read di right end mark 8 as e be
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Di left end no dey at 0 but you read only di right end. Remember wetin Doyun talk earlier.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Adding di two marks no give di length. Di length na di distance between both marks.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Count how many 1cm spaces dey from mark 3 to 8
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You count di spaces between both ends yourself.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Subtract di smaller mark from di bigger mark
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You find di distance between both marks as di difference.
x-m-e2-07.s.s1.reflect: At first you fit judge by looking at only one end, but after you know di other end mark, you find di length differently. When you measure length, always check where both ends dey.
x-m-e2-07.s.s2.prompt: One end of pencil dey at mark a and di other at mark b. Find three different cases where di pencil length na 6cm and left end no dey mark 0. (Ruler marks go from 0 to 15.)
x-m-e2-07.s.s2.hint.0: Right end mark minus left end mark must equal 6.
x-m-e2-07.s.s2.hint.1: Choose di left end mark first, then check whether right end still inside di ruler.
x-m-e2-07.s.s2.ok.c1: Both marks dey on ruler and left end no be 0.
x-m-e2-07.s.s2.fail.c1: Left end mark must be 1 or more and right end mark must be whole number 15 or less.
x-m-e2-07.s.s2.fail.c2: Check whether 6 spaces dey between di marks. Try subtracting left end from right end.
x-m-e2-07.s.s2.explain: If left end na 1, right end na 7; if left na 2, right na 8; if left na 9, right na 15. Any left mark from 1 to 9 give pencil length 6cm.

x-m-e2-08.title: What time di movie go end?
x-m-e2-08.goal: Find di mistake for solution wey find end time with rule say 60 minutes na 1 hour, then make your own showing time wey meet di conditions.
x-m-e2-08.material: Movie start for theater at 1:40. Showing time na 2 hours 30 minutes. Read Ido solution.
x-m-e2-08.thinking.0: Find di First Wrong Line in Solution
x-m-e2-08.thinking.1: Explain di Cause of di Mistake with Time Rules
x-m-e2-08.thinking.2: Make Different Showing Times Wey Meet di Conditions
x-m-e2-08.prereq.0: How to read clock, know how many minutes dey in 1 hour, read times wey mix hours and minutes (Grade 2 level)
x-m-e2-08.s.s1.prompt: Choose di line where Ido solution first go wrong. (Count lines from line 1.)
x-m-e2-08.s.s1.hint.0: Read di time on each line aloud.
x-m-e2-08.s.s1.hint.1: Check one by one whether di time for each line na time wey clock fit show.
x-m-e2-08.s.s1.line.0: Movie start at 1:40 and show for 2 hours 30 minutes. Find di end time.
x-m-e2-08.s.s1.line.3: So di movie go end at 3:70.
x-m-e2-08.s.s1.explain: Di first mistake dey for line 3. 20 minutes after 3:40 na 4:00, and 10 more minutes make am 4:10. When minutes reach 60, you must rewrite dem as 1 hour, so time like “70 minutes” no dey. Line 4 just copy di wrong time from line 3 as conclusion.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.prompt: Movie start at 1:40. Choose showing time so end time exactly 4:00 or later but before 5:00. Find three different examples where showing time na h hours m minutes. (m from 0 to 59.)
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.hint.0: First find how many hours and minutes dey from 1:40 to 4:00, and how long to 5:00.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.hint.1: Choose di hours h for showing time first, then check whether minutes m dey inside correct range.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.ok.c1: Hours na whole number from 0 to 5.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.fail.c1: Hours must be whole number from 0 to 5.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.fail.c2: Minutes must be from 0 to 59. Write 60 minutes as 1 hour.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.ok.c3: End time na exactly 4:00 or later.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.fail.c3: End time before 4:00. Showing time need to be longer.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.fail.c4: End time na exactly 5:00 or later. Showing time need to be shorter.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.explain: From 1:40 to 4:00 na 2 hours 20 minutes, and to 5:00 na 3 hours 20 minutes. So showing time fit be anything from 2 hours 20 minutes up to less than 3 hours 20 minutes. For example, 2 hours 30 minutes, 2 hours 50 minutes, and 3 hours 10 minutes.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.because.prompt: Explain why you no suppose write minutes as 60 or more, like “2 hours 70 minutes.”
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.because.hint.0: Remember how many minutes e be when clock minute hand go round one time.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.because.hint.1: Think wetin 3:70 go be if you read am on clock.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You write how to change 70 minutes to hours and minutes?
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You talk wetin happen to hours when minutes reach 60?
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.because.model.0: When e reach 60 minutes, e become 1 hour, so you need change 70 minutes to 1 hour 10 minutes.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.because.model.1: 1 hour na 60 minutes, so you fit write only up to 59 minutes. 70 minutes na 1 hour 10 minutes.
x-m-e2-08.s.s2.because.model.2: For clock, 60 minutes na one full turn, so no mark for 70 minutes. Rewrite 70 minutes as 1 hour 10 minutes.

x-m-e2-09.title: Wetin Di Table Fit and No Fit Tell Us

Each Grade 2 student choose only one fruit wey dem wan eat after lunch. Below na survey result.
Fruit: apple, strawberry, grape, tangerine
Number of students wey choose am: 7, 9, 5, 4
(If you show am in graph, strawberry bar longest and tangerine bar shortest.)

x-m-e2-09.thinking.1: Tell Apart Wetin No Dey in Data

x-m-e2-09.s.s1.prompt: Look di table and choose everything wey you fit say correct.
x-m-e2-09.s.s1.hint.0: Check one by one whether di table numbers confirm each statement.
x-m-e2-09.s.s1.hint.1: Mark statements wey include information wey no dey for table (future, dislikes).

x-m-e2-09.s.s1.r.c: If you choose dis option, you treat “choose” and “no like” as same. Think whether table fit tell you which students no like something.

x-m-e2-09.s.s1.explain: Strawberry get most with 9, and apple 7 plus tangerine 4 make 11. Future results, number of students wey no like something, and half of grape (half of 5 no be 4) either no dey for table or wrong.
